title: A Rough Friday on Both Sides of the Pacific
body:
By the time Wall Street opened on Friday, Seoul had already suffered one of its worst sessions of the year. The KOSPI, which had been down more than 5% at one point, closed 3.5% lower at 5,730.74, while the KOSDAQ lost 3.8% to 724.38. The fall was so steep that a trading curb (매매 일시 제한) was triggered. Foreign investors drove the **rout** (대폭락), unloading a net 1.62 trillion won of shares, whereas institutions and individuals bought a combined 1.36 trillion won. Kia, which tumbled 11.7% **in the wake of** its quarterly results, showed how little patience investors have left.

Hours later, the pressure **intensified** in New York. Disappointed by Amazon's earnings of $1.89 per share, below the $1.96 analysts had expected, traders sold technology stocks across the board. The Nasdaq slid 2.9% and the S&P 500 fell 1.8%, as the VIX jumped 12.9% to 19.42. Even gold dropped 3.6%, suggesting that some investors were raising cash rather than simply hiding in safe assets.

The **drawdown** (고점 대비 하락폭) is now severe: the KOSPI sits 18.2% below its highest close of the past 20 trading days. Although Korean stocks have often **bounced back** from slumps like this, a quick recovery is far from guaranteed. The longer foreign **outflows** last, the harder it becomes for local buyers to absorb them, and a **prolonged** slide would test even patient investors. Consequently, Apple's results, due after Monday's US close, may matter more than usual.
ko:
금요일 월가가 문을 열 무렵, 서울은 이미 올해 최악의 장 가운데 하나를 겪은 뒤였다. 한때 5% 넘게 빠졌던 코스피는 3.5% 내린 5,730.74로 마감했고, 코스닥은 3.8% 떨어진 724.38을 기록했다. 하락이 워낙 가팔라 매매 일시 제한(사이드카)이 발동됐다. 폭락을 이끈 건 외국인으로, 1조 6,200억 원어치를 순매도했다. 반면 기관과 개인은 합쳐서 1조 3,600억 원을 순매수했다. 분기 실적 발표 직후 11.7% 급락한 기아는 투자자들의 인내심이 얼마나 바닥났는지 보여 줬다.

몇 시간 뒤 뉴욕에서는 압박이 더 거세졌다. 아마존의 주당순이익이 1.89달러로 애널리스트 예상치 1.96달러에 못 미치자 실망한 트레이더들은 기술주를 전반적으로 팔았다. 나스닥은 2.9%, S&P500은 1.8% 하락했고, VIX(공포지수)는 12.9% 뛴 19.42를 기록했다. 금값마저 3.6% 떨어졌는데, 이는 일부 투자자가 단순히 안전자산으로 피신한 게 아니라 현금을 마련하고 있었음을 시사한다.

이제 고점 대비 하락폭은 심각하다. 코스피는 최근 20거래일 최고 종가보다 18.2% 낮은 곳에 있다. 한국 증시는 이런 급락에서 자주 반등해 왔지만, 빠른 회복은 결코 보장되지 않는다. 외국인 자금 유출이 오래 이어질수록 국내 매수세가 이를 받아 내기는 더 어려워지고, 하락이 길어지면 참을성 있는 투자자도 시험대에 오를 것이다. 그래서 월요일 미국 장 마감 뒤 나오는 애플 실적이 평소보다 더 중요할 수 있다.

vocab.en_easy: A sudden, heavy fall in prices when many people sell at once.
vocab.ex: The tech rout wiped out a month of gains in just two days.

vocab.en_easy: How far something has fallen from its highest point.
vocab.ex: My portfolio's drawdown this month is about 10%, so I'm not adding risk yet.

vocab.en_easy: Money moving out of a market, fund, or country.
vocab.ex: Foreign outflows usually push the won weaker and Korean stocks lower.

vocab.en_easy: To become stronger or more extreme.
vocab.ex: The rain intensified halfway through my run, so I cut it short.

vocab.en_easy: Lasting longer than usual or longer than expected.
vocab.ex: After a prolonged break from the gym, my legs were sore for days.

vocab.en_easy: To return to a good condition after a bad period.
vocab.ex: I had a bad cold last week, but I bounced back quickly and went jogging on Saturday.

vocab.en_easy: Right after something happens, usually as a result of it.
vocab.ex: In the wake of the earnings miss, the stock fell 12% in one day.

grammar.point: 과거완료 (had p.p. · by the time + 과거, 주절 had p.p.)
grammar.quote: By the time Wall Street opened on Friday, Seoul had already suffered one of its worst sessions of the year. / The KOSPI, which had been down more than 5% at one point, closed 3.5% lower …
grammar.explain_ko: 과거의 기준 시점(월가 개장·장 마감)보다 '더 먼저' 끝난 일을 had p.p.로 쓴다. by the time + 과거시제 절이 오면 주절은 거의 항상 had p.p.(그때쯤엔 이미 ~했다). 두 번째 인용은 '마감(closed, 과거)' 전에 이미 '5% 넘게 빠져 있었다'는 앞선 상태라 had been. 수능 어법 포인트: 과거 시점 부사(yesterday, last week)와 had p.p.를 섞지 않는다 — 기준 과거가 문장 안에 있을 때만 쓴다.
examples: By the time I checked my account, the market had already closed.
(OPIc) By the time I got to the park, it had already started raining, so I just ran under the bridge.

grammar.point: 비교급 응용 (the + 비교급 ~, the + 비교급 … / as ~ as)
grammar.quote: The longer foreign outflows last, the harder it becomes for local buyers to absorb them …
grammar.explain_ko: '~할수록 더 …하다'. 두 절 모두 'the + 비교급'으로 시작하고, 뒤에 주어 + 동사가 온다(The longer outflows last ✓). 최상급(the hardest)이나 원급(the hard)으로 바꾸면 틀린다 — 수능 어법 단골. 같은 정도는 as + 원급 + as(not as steep as = ~만큼 가파르지 않은).
examples: The more you trade on emotion, the more you tend to lose.
(OPIc) Honestly, the more I run, the better I sleep — it's not as hard as it sounds once you build the habit.

tense.sentence: By the time Wall Street opened on Friday, Seoul had already suffered one of its worst sessions of the year.
tense.why_ko: 월가 개장(과거 기준점)보다 서울 장의 급락이 먼저 끝났으므로 had p.p. — by the time + 과거와 짝.

tense.sentence: Although Korean stocks have often bounced back from slumps like this, a quick recovery is far from guaranteed.
tense.why_ko: 과거부터 지금까지 '여러 번 반등해 온' 경험은 have p.p.(특정 과거 시점이 없음), 지금 판단(보장되지 않는다)은 현재시제.

review.q: After the bank cut its profit forecast, its shares ______ and slipped 4% in early trading.
review.exp_ko: come under pressure = 압박을 받다(하락 압력). 전망을 낮춘 뒤 4% 밀렸으니 '압박을 받았다'. come into play(작용하기 시작하다)는 주어가 '요인'일 때, come in handy(쓸모 있다)는 물건·기술에, come to terms (with)(받아들이다)는 사람이 현실을 받아들일 때라 주가와 안 맞는다.

review.q: 다음 문장과 뜻이 가장 가까운 것은? "The central bank left the door open to another rate cut in December."
choices: The central bank ruled out any rate cut in December.
The central bank said another rate cut in December is still possible.
The central bank already cut rates again in December.
The central bank refused to talk about rates until December.
review.exp_ko: leave the door open to ~ = ~의 가능성을 열어 두다. ①은 '배제했다'로 정반대, ③은 이미 실행(시점 오류), ④는 '말을 안 했다'로 가능성 언급 자체가 없다.

review.q: Higher fuel prices will ______ airlines' profits this quarter, even if ticket sales stay strong.
review.exp_ko: eat into = (이익·저축을) 야금야금 갉아먹다. 연료비 상승이 이익을 줄이는 상황. account for(차지하다·설명하다)는 '이익을 차지하다'로 뜻이 안 맞고, cash in on(~로 이득을 보다)·stock up on(사재기하다)은 even if 양보 논리와 연결이 안 된다.

quiz.q:
[어휘] 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 문맥상 가장 적절한 것은?
"Kia's shares tumbled 11.7% ______ the quarterly results it had released earlier that day, as investors rushed to sell."
quiz.exp_ko: 실적을 '이미 발표한(had released)' 직후의 급락이므로 '~의 여파로' = in the wake of. on the verge of(막 ~하려는 참에)는 아직 일어나지 않은 일에, at the expense of(~을 희생하여)는 대가 관계에, in the course of(~하는 동안)는 진행 중인 과정에 쓰여 '발표 후 반응'이라는 순서와 맞지 않는다.

quiz.q:
[어법] 다음 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?
"By the time Wall Street opened, Seoul ①had already suffered a steep loss. The KOSPI, ②which had fallen more than 5% at one point, closed 3.5% lower. ③Disappointed by Amazon's results, traders sold tech shares, and the longer the outflows continue, ④the hardest it becomes to absorb them."
quiz.exp_ko: 'the + 비교급, the + 비교급' 구문이므로 the hardest(최상급) ✗ → the harder ✓. ① by the time + 과거 → 주절 과거완료 ✓ ② 콤마 뒤 계속적 용법 which ✓(that 불가) ③ 트레이더가 '실망한' 수동 관계라 과거분사 Disappointed ✓.

quiz.q: [요지] 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은? (본문 전체)
choices: Korean stocks fell more than US stocks because Apple's results were weaker than investors expected.
Gold's sharp decline shows that investors have stopped worrying about risk in global markets.
Heavy selling hit both Seoul and New York, and a quick recovery is uncertain if foreign outflows persist.
Because Korean stocks have bounced back before, investors can safely expect a rebound this week.
quiz.exp_ko: 글의 축은 '서울·뉴욕 동반 급락 → 외국인 유출이 길어지면 빠른 회복은 보장 안 됨'. ① 애플 실적은 아직 발표 전(due after Monday's close) ✗ ② 본문은 금 하락을 '현금 마련'으로 해석했지 위험 걱정이 사라졌다는 게 아님 ✗ ④ 'far from guaranteed'와 정반대로 과장 ✗.

quiz.q: [내용 일치·추론] 본문의 숫자로 판단할 때 옳은 것은?
choices: Foreign net selling was larger than the combined net buying of institutions and individuals.
The KOSDAQ fell less than the KOSPI in percentage terms on Friday.
The Nasdaq's decline was more than twice as large as the S&P 500's.
Amazon's earnings per share beat analysts' expectations by 7 cents.
quiz.exp_ko: 외국인 순매도 1.62조 > 기관+개인 순매수 1.36조 ✓. ② 코스닥 −3.8%가 코스피 −3.5%보다 더 많이 빠짐 ✗ ③ 2.9 ÷ 1.8 ≈ 1.6배 — 2배 미만 ✗ ④ 1.89 − 1.96 = −0.07달러, 7센트 '미달'(beat 아님, 방향 함정) ✗.

talk.topic: A sea of red — 코스피 −3.5%, 나스닥 −2.9%: 월요일 아침 어떻게 버티나
talk.setting_ko: 월요일 출근길, 주식 하는 회사 동기(B)와 금요일 급락 얘기를 나누는 상황.

dialogue.en: Did you see Friday? My whole screen was a sea of red.
dialogue.ko: 금요일 봤어? 내 화면이 온통 시뻘겋더라.

dialogue.en: Tell me about it. The KOSPI dropped 3.5%, and then the Nasdaq fell almost 3% that night.
dialogue.ko: 말도 마. 코스피 3.5% 빠지고, 그날 밤 나스닥도 거의 3% 빠졌잖아.

dialogue.en: I'm not gonna lie, I lost sleep over it. I almost sold everything on Saturday morning.
dialogue.ko: 솔직히 그것 때문에 잠을 설쳤어. 토요일 아침에 다 팔 뻔했다니까.

dialogue.en: Glad you didn't. Selling after a drop like that is basically throwing in the towel at the worst time.
dialogue.ko: 안 팔아서 다행이다. 그렇게 빠진 다음에 파는 건 제일 나쁜 타이밍에 백기 드는 거야.

dialogue.en: So what's your plan? Just ride it out?
dialogue.ko: 그럼 넌 어떻게 할 건데? 그냥 버텨?

dialogue.en: Pretty much. I set my rules before the sell-off, so I'll stick to them. Apple reports after the US close today, so we'll know more by tomorrow morning.
dialogue.ko: 거의 그렇지. 급락 전에 규칙을 정해 놨으니 그대로 지킬 거야. 오늘 미국 장 끝나고 애플 실적 나오니까 내일 아침이면 좀 더 알겠지.

dialogue.en: You're right. I need to keep a level head instead of checking my app every five minutes.
dialogue.ko: 맞아. 5분마다 앱 들여다보지 말고 평정심을 유지해야겠다.

expressions.when_ko: 거의 모든 종목이 떨어진 날을 과장해서 말할 때 (미국은 하락=빨강)
expressions.ex: When I opened my app, it was a sea of red.

expressions.when_ko: 걱정이 클 때 / 부정문으로 '그렇게 걱정 안 해'
expressions.ex: I wouldn't lose sleep over one bad day in the market.

expressions.when_ko: 버티던 걸 그만둘 때 (권투에서 수건 던지기)
expressions.ex: I almost threw in the towel on running, but I'm glad I didn't.
The storm was too strong to go out, so we just rode it out at home.
You have to keep a level head when prices swing like this.

your_turn.q_en: Have you ever made a decision you regretted because you were panicking? What had happened before you made it?
your_turn.hint_ko: 과거완료로 배경(I had just ~ / By the time I ~, …had …) → 무엇을 했는지 → 지금 깨달은 점(Now I know ~) / ride it out, keep a level head 활용
your_turn.sample_answer: Yeah, actually. Last year, my phone screen cracked right before an important trip, and by the time I noticed, the repair shops had already closed. I panicked and bought a brand-new phone at the airport, which was way too expensive. If I had kept a level head, I could've just used my old phone for a few days and ridden it out. Now I know that the more stressed I am, the worse my decisions get, so I try to wait at least a day before spending big money.

talk.topic: 한강공원 피크닉 — 자리 잡기, 대여 자전거 펑크 (Background Survey #6 공원 가기)
talk.setting_ko: 토요일 오후, 친구(B)와 한강공원에 피크닉을 갔는데 빌린 자전거 하나가 펑크 난 상황.

dialogue.en: Wow, it's a perfect day for a picnic. Let's grab a spot under that tree before it fills up.
dialogue.ko: 와, 피크닉하기 딱 좋은 날이다. 저 나무 밑 자리 차기 전에 잡자.

dialogue.en: Good call. I'll lay out the mat. Did you bring the snacks?
dialogue.ko: 좋아. 내가 돗자리 깔게. 간식 챙겨 왔어?

dialogue.en: Yep, chicken's on the way, too. Oh no — I think my bike has a flat.
dialogue.ko: 응, 치킨도 오는 중이야. 아 이런, 내 자전거 바퀴 펑크 난 것 같아.

dialogue.en: Seriously? We rented them, like, twenty minutes ago.
I know. I'll call the rental place and ask if they can swap it.
dialogue.ko: 그러니까. 대여소에 전화해서 바꿔 줄 수 있는지 물어볼게.

dialogue.en: If it takes too long, let's just walk along the river instead. We can take a rain check on the bike ride.
dialogue.ko: 너무 오래 걸리면 그냥 강 따라 걷자. 자전거는 다음에 타면 되지.

dialogue.en: Deal. The weather's this nice, so let's make the most of it either way.
dialogue.ko: 좋아. 날씨가 이렇게 좋으니까 어쨌든 최대한 즐기자.

expressions.when_ko: 날씨 묘사로 대화를 시작할 때 (OPIc 공원·여행 도입에도 좋음)
expressions.ex: It's a perfect day for a long walk by the river.
Let's get there early and grab a spot near the stage.

expressions.when_ko: 자전거·차 타이어 문제를 말할 때 (OPIc 롤플레이 문제해결에 활용)
expressions.ex: I had a flat on my way home, so I had to walk the bike.
Can I take a rain check on dinner? I have to work late.

expressions.when_ko: 좋은 기회·시간을 충분히 누리자고 할 때
expressions.ex: I only had one day off, so I tried to make the most of it.

your_turn.q_en: What do you usually do when you go to a park? Tell me about the last time you went.
your_turn.hint_ko: 루틴(현재: I usually ~) → 지난번(과거: Last Saturday, I ~ / by the time ~ had ~) → 느낌·다음 계획 / grab a spot, make the most of 활용
your_turn.sample_answer: I usually go to the park near my place to walk or jog, but on weekends I sometimes have a picnic with friends. The last time I went was a few weeks ago. It was a perfect day for it, so by the time we got there, most of the shady spots had already been taken. We finally grabbed a spot near the river, ordered some chicken, and just talked for hours. It was super relaxing, so I'm planning to go again before it gets too cold.

opic.survey_topic: 조깅 (Background Survey #46) · 월요일 콤보: 묘사 → 루틴 → 과거 경험

combo.q_en: In the survey, you indicated that you go jogging. Where do you usually go jogging? Please describe the place in as much detail as possible.
combo.q_ko: 서베이에서 조깅을 한다고 하셨네요. 보통 어디서 조깅하나요? 그 장소를 최대한 자세히 묘사해 주세요.
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(장소 한 줄: 이름·집에서 거리) → 본문 2~3포인트: ①보이는 것(코스 길이·바닥·강·나무) ②사람·분위기(시간대별) ③내가 좋아하는 이유(감정) → 마무리(그래서 거의 매일 간다). 90초. 채점 포인트: 형용사·위치 표현(along, next to, on one side)으로 그림 그리기, 현재시제 일관, 'There is/are' 반복 피하기.
combo.model_answer: Okay, so the place I usually go jogging is a river park, which is about ten minutes from my apartment on foot. I'd like to talk about the path first. There's a long running track along the river — it's about five kilometers one way — and the ground is that soft, rubbery material, so it's really easy on your knees. On one side, you've got the river, and on the other side, there are rows of trees and some benches. Um, at night, the bridges light up, and honestly, it looks pretty amazing. What I like most about it is the atmosphere. In the evening, it's full of people — runners, couples walking their dogs, kids on bikes — but it never feels too crowded, because the path is so wide. And there are convenience stores and public restrooms here and there, so I don't have to carry much. You know, it's just a really comfortable place. That's why I end up going there almost every day.

key_phrases.en: The place I usually go ~ing is ~
On one side, ~ and on the other side, ~

combo.level_up_ko: IM은 'It is big. It is nice.' 나열, IH는 위치 표현으로 공간을 그리듯 묘사, AL은 시간대별 변화(낮 vs 밤)와 '왜 좋은지'를 감정과 함께 문단으로 묶는다.

combo.q_en: Tell me about your typical jogging routine. When do you usually go, how long do you run, and what do you do before and after you jog?
combo.q_ko: 평소 조깅 루틴을 말해 주세요. 보통 언제 가고, 얼마나 뛰고, 조깅 전후에 무엇을 하나요?
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(It goes something like this: 순서 예고) → 본문: ①전(시간·워밍업 — 동적 스트레칭, 근육 이름) ②중(거리·페이스·음악) ③후(쿨다운·폼롤러·샤워·단백질) → 마무리(이 루틴이 생긴 뒤 달라진 점). 90초~2분. 채점 포인트: first/then/after that/once ~ 연결어, 현재시제 습관 + 빈도부사, 헬스 서베이와 같은 근육 어휘로 구체성 확보.
combo.model_answer: Sure. It goes something like this: I usually go jogging right after work, around seven, three or four times a week. Before I start, I always do some dynamic stretching for about five minutes — like leg swings and walking lunges — to warm up my hamstrings and hip flexors. I used to skip that part, but my calves got tight all the time, so now I never skip it. Then I run about five kilometers at an easy pace. I try to keep my heart rate in a comfortable zone, you know, where I can still talk. I always listen to a playlist with fast beats, because it helps me keep a steady rhythm. Once I'm done, I walk for a few minutes to cool down, and then I stretch my quads and calves. When I get home, I use a foam roller, take a shower, and have a protein shake. Honestly, the more consistent I am with this routine, the better I feel during the day. It's become a big part of my life.

key_phrases.en: warm up my hamstrings and hip flexors

combo.level_up_ko: IM은 'I run. I go home.' 단문, IH는 연결어로 전·중·후 순서를 잇기, AL은 used to → now로 루틴이 바뀐 이유(종아리가 뭉쳐서)를 끼워 시제 전환을 보여 준다.

combo.q_en: Tell me about a memorable experience you had while jogging. Maybe something unexpected or funny happened. What happened, and why was it so memorable?
combo.q_ko: 조깅하다가 있었던 기억에 남는 경험을 말해 주세요. 예상 못 했거나 웃긴 일일 수도 있겠죠. 무슨 일이었고, 왜 그렇게 기억에 남나요?
combo.strategy_ko: 도입(언제·어디서 한 줄) → 본문: ①배경(과거진행·과거완료: I was running ~ / I had already run ~) ②사건(Out of nowhere, ~ — 대화체 인용 넣기) ③결과·감정 → 마무리(그 뒤로 달라진 습관). 2분. 채점 포인트: 과거·과거진행·과거완료를 섞어 시간 순서를 정확히, 직접 화법으로 생동감, 자기수정(Actually, no, wait ~).
combo.model_answer: Oh, I've got one. This was last summer, on a really hot evening. I was running along the river, and by the time I got to the halfway point, I had already finished my water. So I was pretty exhausted. Then, out of nowhere, a guy on a bike stopped next to me and said, "Hey, you dropped this!" It was my phone — it had slipped out of my pocket, like, a kilometer back, and I hadn't even noticed. I was so shocked, I just stood there for a second. Then I thanked him like five times. Actually, no, wait — I think I even tried to give him my energy bar, and he laughed and said, "Keep it, you look like you need it more." I couldn't stop laughing, because he was totally right. Anyway, it was memorable because it reminded me that people can be really kind. And ever since then, I always zip my pocket before I start running.

key_phrases.en: by the time I got to ~, I had already ~

combo.level_up_ko: IM은 사건만 한 줄, IH는 배경-사건-결과 3단으로 이야기 만들기, AL은 과거완료(had slipped, hadn't noticed)로 '앞선 일'을 정확히 깔고 직접 화법·자기수정으로 원어민 같은 흐름을 보여 준다.

useful.en: I'd like to talk about ~ first.
useful.when_ko: 묘사 문항에서 순서를 정하며 시작할 때

useful.en: What I like most about it is ~

useful.when_ko: 경험 이야기를 '지금 달라진 점'으로 마무리할 때

opic.practice_ko: 3문항을 쉬지 않고 이어서 녹음(각 90초~2분). 다시 들으며 ①과거 경험에서 had p.p.를 최소 1번 썼는지 ②루틴에서 근육 이름 2개 이상 넣었는지 체크하고, 빠졌으면 그 부분만 한 번 더 녹음.

aptitude.q: 10월 30일 코스피에서 외국인은 1조 6,169억 원을 순매도했고, 기관은 7,432억 원, 개인은 6,199억 원을 순매수했다. 순매수한 두 주체(기관+개인)의 순매수 합에서 기관이 차지하는 비중에 가장 가까운 것은?
10월 30일 코스피는 전일 대비 3.48% 내린 5,730.74로 마감했다. 전일(10월 29일) 종가에 가장 가까운 것은?
10월 30일 코스피 종가 5,730.74는 최근 20거래일 최고 종가 7,003.74보다 18.2% 낮다. 코스피가 이 최고 종가를 다시 회복하려면 10월 30일 종가 대비 몇 % 올라야 하는가?
